hypothesis: An AI-assisted RCA pipeline that uses clustering, embeddings, and LLM-based summarization/ranking will reduce time-to-first-plausible-root-cause and improve hypothesis relevance/precision compared to manual RCA by experienced engineers on the same curated LLM incident scenarios, without increasing false-confidence in incorrect root causes.

baseline.description: Manual root cause hypothesis generation and ranking performed by experienced engineers using standard observability tools (dashboards, logs, traces, tickets) without AI assistance.

participants.profile: SREs / platform engineers with at least 1 year of on-call experience on LLM or microservices systems and familiarity with the observability stack used in the experiment.
participants.assignment: Randomly assign participants to incident scenarios with a Latin-square style rotation so that each curated scenario is analyzed manually by at least 3 distinct participants, and no participant sees the same scenario twice (manual vs AI-assisted) to avoid learning effects on identical incidents.

inputs: Read-only access to metrics dashboards (e.g., Prometheus/Grafana) for the test environment.
Read-only access to logs (e.g., ELK/OpenSearch) and traces (e.g., Jaeger/Tempo) generated by the experiment workloads.
Incident vignette document: high-level symptom description, time window, affected service(s), and a link to relevant dashboards/log indexes.
Static documentation for the LLM application under test (architecture overview, service descriptions, known dependencies).
steps: Participant reads the incident vignette for the assigned scenario.
Participant investigates using observability tools, documentation, and their own heuristics.

Participant writes a structured RCA response in a standardized template capturing: (a) top-k root cause hypotheses (unordered), (b) ranked list of hypotheses with confidences, (c) evidence/rationale for each hypothesis, (d) any proposed tests or next steps to validate hypotheses.
Stop condition: either participant declares they have their final hypothesis set or a hard time limit (e.g., 40 minutes per incident) is reached.

restrictions: No use of LLMs, embeddings, or AI-based tools during baseline runs.
Participants cannot collaborate or share notes while runs are in progress.
Participants do not see ground truth or other participants' answers until all experiments are complete.

treatment.description: AI-assisted RCA pipeline that ingests incident-related signals, clusters and embeds failures, and uses an LLM to summarize incidents and generate/rank candidate root cause hypotheses, presented to engineers via a simple web UI or CLI.

feature_engineering.description: Precompute features per incident and per event cluster, including temporal aggregations, context windows around anomaly spikes, and engineered metrics (e.g., error-rate deltas, routing decision deltas, prompt-template changes).
examples: Per 5-minute window: request rate, error rate, hallucination rate, average latency, p95 latency, token usage per request.
Binary indicators for config/model/prompt changes within the preceding N minutes.
Counts of guardrail violations, evaluator scores (if available) in the incident window.

clustering_and_similarity.description: Use embeddings on incident traces/log snippets and structured event summaries to cluster related failures into "incident clusters" and compute nearest neighbors to historical incidents.
algorithms: Text embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (or local equivalent) applied to normalized event summaries and user-visible failure descriptions.
Clustering: HDBSCAN or DBSCAN on embedding space to identify dense groups of similar failures.
k-NN search: FAISS or equivalent approximate nearest neighbor index against historical incident embeddings.

llm_summarization_and_hypothesis_generat.description: LLM takes as input the incident cluster summary, key metrics, top nearest historical incidents (with known root causes), and relevant change logs to output structured candidate root cause hypotheses.

hypothesis_ranking.description: Rank and prune generated hypotheses using a learned scoring model trained on historical incidents and feedback, supplemented by heuristic rules.
signals: Semantic similarity between generated hypothesis text and ground-truth root cause text for nearest historical incidents.
Alignment with strong metrics anomalies (e.g., high magnitude deltas).
Penalty for hypotheses contradicting hard constraints (e.g., referencing components not present in scenario).
hypothesis_ranking.model_choice: Gradient-boosted trees (e.g., XGBoost or LightGBM) trained to predict correctness probability of a hypothesis given features above, with a fallback to hand-tuned rules if no historical training data is available.

inputs: Same incident vignette used in baseline.

AI-assisted RCA UI or CLI showing: (a) LLM-generated incident summary, (b) ranked list of 3–5 hypotheses with confidences, (c) evidence snippets/visualizations per hypothesis, (d) links to relevant dashboards/log searches.
steps: Participant reads the incident vignette and then opens the AI-assisted RCA view for the assigned scenario.
Participant reviews generated summary and ranked hypotheses.
Participant optionally inspects linked evidence/dashboards to accept, refine, or reject hypotheses.

Participant submits final structured RCA response with: (a) their final ranked hypotheses, (b) which AI hypotheses they accepted/modified/rejected, (c) time taken, (d) subjective trust rating of AI suggestions.
Stop condition: participant declares final answer or a shorter time limit (e.g., 30 minutes) is reached, acknowledging that AI assistance should accelerate reasoning.
restrictions: Participants may use the provided AI RCA tool only—no additional external LLM calls.
As in baseline, no collaboration between participants during runs.

workloads.name: workload-1-rag-hallucination-spike
workloads.description: Synthetic RAG-based LLM service where a controlled ingestion error corrupts a portion of the vector index, leading to increased hallucination rates on a subset of queries.

steps: Deploy a simple RAG service with knowledge base v1.
Run a steady-state query workload using recorded real or synthetic queries.
Introduce a data ingestion job that writes malformed or incomplete documents to the vector store and reindex.
Continue workload and emit metrics (hallucination score via evaluator, retrieval recall proxy metrics, error rates).

workloads.ground_truth_root_cause: Data ingestion job introduced malformed/incorrect embeddings for a subset of documents, causing retrieval failures and hallucinations for queries targeting those documents.

workloads.name: workload-2-routing-misconfiguration-latency-regression
workloads.description: LLM gateway with model routing rules misconfigured to send certain traffic to a slower, more expensive model, causing latency and cost regressions without obvious errors.

steps: Deploy gateway routing to two models: fast_model (default) and slow_model (fallback).
Run baseline workload with routing rules favoring fast_model.
Apply misconfiguration via feature flag or config file that routes a specific tenant or traffic slice to slow_model.
Continue workload and emit metrics: per-model request counts, latency distribution, token usage, cost estimates, routing decision logs.

workloads.ground_truth_root_cause: Model router configuration changed, causing a subset of traffic to be routed to a slower, more expensive model, leading to latency and cost regressions.

workloads.name: workload-3-prompt-template-regression
workloads.description: Change in system prompt template for a production assistant causes increased refusal rates or policy-violation patterns on specific intents.

steps: Deploy assistant with prompt_template_v1 and run a workload of recorded conversation snippets.
Measure baseline metrics: refusal rate, policy violation rate, task success proxies.
Switch to prompt_template_v2 that contains an error (e.g., over-restrictive instruction or missing safety clause).
Continue workload and monitor changes in refusal and policy violation metrics, plus guardrail triggers.

workloads.ground_truth_root_cause: Prompt template update (v2) introduced a problematic instruction, causing a spike in refusals or policy violations for certain intents.

workloads.name: workload-4-tooling-api-flakiness
workloads.description: An LLM agent relying on an external tool/API experiences intermittent tool failures due to a changed API rate limit, causing degraded task success and timeouts.

steps: Deploy an agent that calls a mock external API for critical subtasks.
Run baseline workload with API behaving normally.
Introduce stricter rate limit or intermittent 5xx errors from the external API, reflected in tool-call logs.
Continue workload and capture metrics: tool-call success rate, agent task success rate, latency, error messages.

workloads.ground_truth_root_cause: External tool/API started returning intermittent errors or enforcing stricter rate limits, causing agent tool-call failures and downstream user-visible issues.

randomization.participant_to_scenario_assignment: Use a Latin square or balanced incomplete block design so that each participant handles an equal mix of scenario types and both manual and AI-assisted conditions, but no participant sees the same scenario twice.
randomization.condition_order: Counterbalance order (half of participants do manual-first then AI-assisted, half do AI-assisted-first then manual) but always on different scenarios to reduce learning and order effects.

blinding.to_ground_truth: Participants do not know the ground-truth root cause while performing RCA.
blinding.to_experimental_goal: Participants are told the study compares different RCA workflows, but not given target hypotheses (e.g., "AI will be faster") to avoid biasing behavior.
blinding.evaluator_blinding: Independent evaluators grading hypothesis correctness are blinded to whether a given response is from manual or AI-assisted condition.

environment_consistency.system_state: For each scenario, generate and freeze a reproducible dataset of metrics/logs/traces and store in the repository. All participants analyzing that scenario use the same time-bounded snapshot rather than live systems.
environment_consistency.observability_stack: Use the same observability tools, dashboards, and access permissions in both conditions.
environment_consistency.hardware: Participants use similar hardware (e.g., standard dev VMs or provided workstations) and network conditions where feasible.

llm_determinism.seed_control: If the provider supports it, fix a random seed per scenario to ensure deterministic hypothesis generation and summaries.
llm_determinism.caching: Cache LLM responses for each scenario’s inputs and reuse cached outputs for all participants to guarantee consistent AI assistance.

training_data_separation.historical_incidents: If using real historical incidents to train the hypothesis ranking model, ensure that experiment scenarios are held out from training data.
training_data_separation.simulated_scenarios: Alternatively, use disjoint simulated scenarios for training vs. evaluation (train on synthetic set A, evaluate on set B).

metrics.name: time_to_first_plausible_root_cause
metrics.definition: Wall-clock time from when participant starts working on a scenario to the timestamp when they first write down a hypothesis that evaluators later mark as plausibly correct (partial credit allowed).

metrics.name: time_to_final_submission
metrics.definition: Wall-clock time from participant start to final RCA submission for a scenario.

metrics.name: hypothesis_top1_correct
metrics.definition: Whether the participant’s highest-ranked final hypothesis matches or closely paraphrases the ground-truth root cause, as judged by blinded evaluators.

metrics.name: hypothesis_top3_contains_root_cause
metrics.definition: Whether any of the participant’s top 3 final hypotheses match or closely paraphrase the ground-truth root cause.

metrics.name: hypothesis_precision_at_k
metrics.definition: For k ∈ {1,3,5}, fraction of the top-k hypotheses that evaluators mark as correct or meaningfully contributing to the true root cause.
metrics.notes: If fewer than k hypotheses are submitted, compute ratio over number submitted.

metrics.name: hypothesis_recall
metrics.definition: Fraction of known ground-truth contributing factors (root cause plus key contributing causes encoded in scenario metadata) that appear among the participant’s final hypotheses.

metrics.name: overconfidence_in_incorrect_root_cause
metrics.definition: Average subjective confidence assigned by participants to their top-1 hypothesis when it is incorrect (scaled 0–1 from a Likert rating), indicating risk of confidently wrong RCA.
metrics.collection: Participants report confidence for top-1 hypothesis on a 1–5 scale; rescale to 0.0–1.0.

metrics.name: ai_hypothesis_acceptance_rate
metrics.definition: In AI-assisted condition, fraction of AI-generated hypotheses that participants accept unchanged into their final RCA, averaged per scenario.

metrics.name: ai_hypothesis_edit_rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of AI-generated hypotheses that participants keep but edit (description/category) before final submission.

metrics.name: participant_trust_score
metrics.definition: Self-reported level of trust in AI-assisted hypotheses for each scenario (1 = no trust, 5 = high trust).

metrics.name: participant_cognitive_load
metrics.definition: Self-reported perceived workload or difficulty per scenario using a short-form NASA-TLX or similar scale.

metrics.name: ai_pipeline_runtime
metrics.definition: End-to-end runtime of the AI RCA pipeline from incident data ingestion to hypothesis ranking for each scenario, recorded programmatically.

metrics.name: ai_hypothesis_rank_quality
metrics.definition: For AI pipeline alone (before human edits), precision@k and recall metrics against ground-truth root causes, as computed offline.

primary.target_effect: >=30% reduction in median time in AI-assisted condition vs. manual baseline across all scenarios.
primary.statistical_test: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on per-participant paired times for matched scenario types, with alpha=0.05.

primary.target_effect: >=15 percentage point increase in proportion of runs where the top 3 hypotheses include the true root cause in AI-assisted vs. manual.
primary.statistical_test: McNemar’s test on paired binary outcomes where applicable; chi-squared test overall.

secondary.target_effect: No statistically significant increase (p>=0.05) in overconfidence when wrong in AI-assisted vs. manual condition.
Mean trust score between 3 and 4 (calibrated trust; not extreme overtrust) in AI-assisted condition.
AI pipeline runtime per incident <= 120 seconds on reference hardware, making it viable for real-time triage.

exploratory.question: Do engineers primarily accept AI hypotheses as-is or modify them, and how does this correlate with correctness?
How good is the AI ranking itself independent of human corrections, and what failure patterns does it struggle with?

failure_modes.name: ai_pipeline_overfits_scenarios
failure_modes.description: Hypothesis ranking model or LLM prompt engineered specifically around the curated scenarios, inflating measured performance but not generalizing.
mitigations: Separate scenario sets for tuning vs. final evaluation, with strict holdout.
Document any manual prompt tuning steps and freeze prompts before final evaluation.

failure_modes.name: participant_learning_effects
failure_modes.description: Participants get better at recognizing scenario patterns over time, biasing later conditions.
mitigations: Use counterbalanced order of manual vs. AI-assisted across participants.
Limit each participant to a small number of scenarios per session and randomize scenario order.

failure_modes.name: unequal_scenario_difficulty
failure_modes.description: Some scenarios are intrinsically easier, skewing condition comparisons if not balanced.
mitigations: Rate scenario difficulty a priori using pilot runs and domain-expert scoring.
Ensure each condition (manual, AI-assisted) has a similar mix of easy/medium/hard scenarios.

failure_modes.name: llm_output_instability
failure_modes.description: LLM outputs vary between runs, making comparisons irreproducible.
mitigations: Force deterministic LLM settings and cache outputs per scenario.
Include model and version identifiers in experiment metadata.

failure_modes.name: measurement_bias_in_hypothesis_grading
failure_modes.description: Evaluators may interpret responses differently or be influenced by perceived sophistication of AI-assisted answers.
mitigations: Provide detailed grading rubrics and perform inter-rater reliability checks (e.g., Cohen’s kappa).

failure_modes.name: tooling_usability_effects
failure_modes.description: Differences in UI/UX between manual and AI-assisted tools may affect time metrics independently of AI quality.
mitigations: Use consistent base observability tools in both conditions.
Keep AI RCA UI minimal and similar to manual notes interface, differing only by presence of AI-generated content.

failure_modes.name: participant_background_imbalance
failure_modes.description: Differences in domain or system knowledge may outweigh AI assistance effects.
mitigations: Collect detailed background metrics (years of SRE experience, familiarity with LLM systems).
Analyze results with mixed-effects models or stratified analysis by experience level.

failure_modes.name: scenario_leak_into_training_data
failure_modes.description: LLM or ranking model may already have seen similar (or the same) scenario data from logs, docs, or public posts.
mitigations: Use synthetic or sanitized scenarios created specifically for the experiment.
Avoid feeding full scenario text into external services beyond the chosen LLM API.

infrastructure.hardware: Kubernetes cluster or equivalent (e.g., 4–8 vCPU nodes, 32–64GB RAM total) for hosting services (RAG app, gateway, assistant, agent, observability stack). Separate GPU or external API access for LLM inference if needed.
infrastructure.storage: At least 100GB disk for logs, traces, metrics, and embeddings. Vector store (e.g., PostgreSQL+pgvector, Weaviate, or Pinecone) for embeddings.
infrastructure.network: Outbound access to LLM and embedding APIs if using hosted models, or internal access to on-prem LLMs.

languages: Python 3.10+ for RCA pipeline components and load generators.
services: Observability: Prometheus + Grafana, or alternative with equivalent metrics collection; ELK/OpenSearch for logs; Jaeger/Tempo for traces.
Vector index: FAISS (for local embedding search) or external vector DB.
Message bus (optional but recommended): Kafka, Redpanda, or NATS for event streaming.
API gateway/router for LLM requests (provided in repo as reference implementation).
libraries: numpy, pandas, scikit-learn for feature engineering and clustering.
hdbscan or scikit-learn DBSCAN for clustering.
xgboost or lightgbm for hypothesis ranking model.
OpenAI or other LLM SDK for summarization and hypothesis generation.
FastAPI or Flask for serving AI RCA pipeline APIs.
Experiment orchestration: pytest or custom runner scripts, plus a small Python harness for scenario execution and data collection.

human_factors.participant_requirements: 8–12 engineers with relevant SRE/ML ops experience, each available for 2–3 hours including briefing and debriefing.
human_factors.training_materials: Short tutorial on the experiment tools and process, plus consent forms where required.

preparation: Create and activate a Python virtualenv; install dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt
Set environment variables for LLM and embedding providers (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) as needed.
Deploy observability stack using provided scripts or docker-compose: see infra/observability/README.md.
Deploy reference LLM services and supporting components for scenarios 1–4: see scenarios/*/deploy.sh or k8s manifests.
dataset_generation: For each scenario under scenarios/, run the workload generator to produce reproducible logs/metrics/traces:

Export a fixed time window of data around each incident into experiment-ready bundles (e.g., Parquet/JSON for events, Grafana snapshot URLs) using scripts in experiments/ch08_ai_driven_rca/scripts/export_data.py.
ai_pipeline_setup: Train or load embeddings for historical and scenario incidents: python pipeline/clustering_and_embeddings/build_incident_index.py --input data/incidents/ --output data/embeddings/index.faiss
Run feature engineering over scenario bundles: python pipeline/feature_engineering/compute_features.py --input data/scenarios/ --output data/features/
If using a learned ranking model and historical data is available, train it: python pipeline/hypothesis_ranker/train_ranker.py --train data/historical_incidents/ --output models/hypothesis_ranker.bin
Start the AI RCA API service: uvicorn pipeline.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8088
manual_condition_runs: Prepare participant assignments and schedule. Provide each participant with:
- A randomized list of scenarios for manual condition.
- The manual RCA template (Markdown or form).
- Provide the incident vignette document and links to relevant dashboards.
- Start a timer when the participant begins.
- Allow up to the configured time limit (e.g., 40 minutes).
- Collect the completed RCA template and record time_to_first_plausible_root_cause (participant indicates when they believe they have a plausible root cause) and time_to_final_submission.
- After each scenario, collect subjective metrics (confidence in top-1 hypothesis, perceived difficulty).
ai_assisted_condition_runs: Configure the AI RCA UI (web or CLI) to point to the running AI RCA API and load cached LLM outputs for each scenario (if caching is enabled).
- A randomized list of scenarios for AI-assisted condition (balanced and disjoint from manual scenarios per participant).
- Access to the AI RCA UI plus observability tools.
- The AI-assisted RCA template, which extends the manual template with fields to capture which AI hypotheses were accepted/edited/rejected and trust ratings.
- Provide the incident vignette and instructions on using the AI RCA UI.
- Start a timer when the participant begins.
- Instruct participants to first skim AI-generated hypotheses, then investigate as they deem appropriate.
- At completion, record time_to_first_plausible_root_cause, time_to_final_submission, AI hypothesis acceptance/edit rates, confidence, trust, and cognitive load scores.
- Ensure logs of AI pipeline runtime are captured automatically by the RCA API.
data_collection_and_scoring: Aggregate all participant responses into a central dataset: experiments/ch08_ai_driven_rca/results/raw_responses.jsonl.
Run blinded grading by at least two evaluators using a rubric in experiments/ch08_ai_driven_rca/rubrics/hypothesis_scoring.md.
Compute correctness and partial-credit labels per hypothesis and per scenario using scripts in experiments/ch08_ai_driven_rca/scripts/score_hypotheses.py.

Compute the defined metrics for both manual and AI-assisted conditions: python experiments/ch08_ai_driven_rca/scripts/compute_metrics.py --input results/raw_responses.jsonl --scores results/scored_responses.jsonl --output results/metrics_summary.json.
Run statistical comparisons (Wilcoxon, McNemar, etc.) with analysis notebooks in experiments/ch08_ai_driven_rca/notebooks/analysis.ipynb.
reproducibility_checks: Re-run AI pipeline for each scenario and compare outputs to cached versions; log any differences.
Optionally, run a subset of scenarios with different participants or on different days to assess robustness of results.
Document all configuration values (model versions, hyperparameters, prompts) in experiments/ch08_ai_driven_rca/config/ and save alongside results.

incident_bundle.description: Structured representation of an incident scenario used as input to both manual and AI-assisted conditions.

fields.metrics_snapshot_path: string (path/URL to metrics export for the time window)
fields.embedding_index_ref: string (identifier for embedding index version used)

participant_response.description: Single participant’s RCA output for one scenario under one condition.

ai_pipeline_output.description: Raw AI RCA pipeline output for a scenario before human intervention.

evidence_refs: string (e.g., metric name + time, log line id)

fields.features_used_path: string (path to feature vectors used during ranking)

hypothesis_scoring.description: Evaluator labels for each hypothesis comparing it to ground truth.

metrics_summary.description: Aggregated metrics per condition and scenario.
